title: Cohort rollup blocking checkout during audit window

brief.headline: both guardians agree the decision belongs to a human
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 1293622 (batch_worker/analytics_cohort_rollup, idle in transaction, txn open 4.2s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 0% over 30s (120/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $18,400/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/analytics_cohort_rollup, pid 1293622) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $18,400/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Checkout at 0% success (BIZ-4) vs 95% SLO, $18,400/min revenue at risk. Waiting would cost ~$305K (996s remaining per BIZ-5) and EXCEEDS 60s tolerance. Terminating costs 20-min replay (BIZ-2). However, active change calendar CHG-6214 mandates consult_owner (BIZ-3): cohort outputs are external audit evidence requiring data owner sign-off. Per I3, this trade-off belongs to the human owner.

audit.report: The analytics_cohort_rollup job (pid 1293622) went idle in transaction (last statement SELECT 1) for 4.2s and blocked all checkout sessions, collapsing checkout success to 0% (120/120 failed over 30s) against a 95% SLO with $18,400/min revenue at risk. Both guardians agreed the trade-off favored termination — waiting would cost ~$305K (996s remaining runtime) versus a 20-minute replay — but change calendar CHG-6214 mandated a consult_owner policy because cohort outputs serve as evidence for an external audit. The negotiation escalated to the data-analytics team for human sign-off; the escalation took 573 seconds, far exceeding the 60-second business tolerance for degraded checkout. The action was not executed automatically, so checkout recovery status is unknown from this trace.
audit.root_cause: The analytics_cohort_rollup job held an idle-in-transaction lock (SELECT 1) during an active audit-window change (CHG-6214), blocking checkout and triggering a consult_owner requirement that forced human escalation while revenue loss accumulated.
lessons: For analytics_cohort_rollup: Add a pre-audit-window check that the job is not idle in transaction (SELECT 1) before CHG-6214 windows open, since the idle state blocked checkout for 573s before escalation.

For analytics_cohort_rollup: Configure idle_in_transaction_session_timeout or statement_timeout to auto-terminate idle transactions, preventing a 996s remaining runtime from blocking revenue-critical checkout.

For analytics_cohort_rollup: Pre-negotiate an interrupt protocol with the data-analytics owner for CHG-6214 audit windows so future escalations don't require 573s of human consultation while checkout is at 0%.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian correctly identified all missing evidence in round 1 and requested the workload registry, protected settlements, change calendar, and impact probes; the continuity guardian accepted the trade-off math (~$305K wait cost vs 20-min replay) but both guardians were constrained by CHG-6214's consult_owner invariant, making escalation the only valid action — no rounds were wasted.
follow_ups: data-analytics owner to confirm whether the analytics_cohort_rollup run can be terminated and replayed (20 min) given CHG-6214 audit evidence requirements.
Review why analytics_cohort_rollup entered idle-in-transaction state (SELECT 1) during the audit window and add guardrails (timeouts, pre-audit completion checks).
Update CHG-6214 change calendar entry with a pre-approved interrupt decision for future audit windows to avoid 573s escalation latency.
